prompt: A die is thrown 200 times and lands on six 41 times. Find the relative frequency of a six and comment on whether the die appears fair.
markscheme: $\dfrac{41}{200}=0.205$ **(A1)**; a fair die gives $\frac16\approx0.167$ (about 33 sixes). 41 is higher, which hints at bias, but more trials would be needed to be confident **(R1)**

prompt: Two fair dice are thrown. Find the probability that the total is 8.
A fair die is rolled 4 times. Find the probability of getting at least one six.
markscheme:
$P(\text{no six})=\left(\tfrac56\right)^{4}$ **(M1)**; $P(\text{at least one})=1-\left(\tfrac56\right)^{4}=\dfrac{671}{1296}\approx0.518$ **(A1)**

“At least one” is almost always easiest through the complement.
